To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the risk reduction with statin treatment in the elderly is related to baseline HDLc but not LDLc, that the change in the ratio of LDLc to HDLc on treatment may be the key determinant of benefit, and that the risk of vascular events in the elderly is not related to LDLc or HDLDc levels but is related to baseline and change in the LDL/HDL ratio.
in the elderly, HDLc, rather than LDLc, is the key predictor of risk of cardiovascular disease and that statin therapy should be targeted to those at risk who have low HDLc levels.
HDLc is a key predictor of both risk and of treatment with statin drugs in people >70 years of age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel therapies for the treatment of cardiovascular disease.
the role of lipids as predictors of risk in the elderly and as predictors of treatment benefit.
the role of lipoproteins and apolipoproteins in vascular disease prevention and in the assessment of treatment benefit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PROSPER trial has shown that in elderly subjects at high risk, pravastatin treatment reduces the risk of coronary heart disease and stroke.
in older patients, statin therapy is beneficial and should not be withheld because of age.
the LDL-C/HDL-C ratio is a useful predictor of cardiovascular risk in older patients, and that the LDL-C level is not a useful predictor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LDLc/HDC ratio appears to be the best predictor of risk in older patients, and the ratio is the best target for statin treatment.
in the elderly, the best predictors of risk are HDLc and the LDLc/Hdlc ratio, and the best predictors of treatment benefit are HDLc, the LDLc/HdLc ratio, and change in the LDL/HDL ratio on treatment.
HDLc is a key determinant of risk in older subjects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in older patients, the best predictors of risk of coronary events are the plasma levels of high-density lipoprotein (HDL) and the ratio of low-density lipoprotein to HDL.
the lipid hypothesis of atherosclerosis is wrong.
HDLc, not LDLc, was a key predictor of cardiovascular risk and of the treatment effect of pravastatin in the elderly.
